title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics + parity + version bump v1.141.0
author: Jordan Park
description:
Motivation: This PR unifies SDK auth/retries behaviour and streaming ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go, fixes several parity gaps, and bumps the public SDK versions to v1.141.0. Key goals: 1) make credential/refresh semantics consistent across languages, 2) centralize retry backoff and idempotency behavior, 3) align streaming API interfaces and docs, and 4) prepare crates/packages for a coordinated version bump. Changes span the monorepo SDK packages and the shared generator templates.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Normalize auth initialization: support scoped token providers, automatic refresh hooks, and clearer SDK-level credential precedence rules.
- Retry policy consolidation: single source-of-truth retry config with exponential backoff + jitter and idempotency hints for idempotent routes.
- Streaming ergonomics: unify chunking callbacks, add an async iterator interface in Python, add an Observable-like wrapper in TypeScript, and add channel-friendly helpers in Go.
- Parity fixes: align Python/TS/Go method names and parameter ordering, fix header propagation for proxy scenarios, and ensure consistent error classes across languages.
- Version bump: package metadata updated to v1.141.0, changelogs for each SDK.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for retry logic in all three SDKs
- [x] End-to-end streaming smoke tests (local runtime)
- [x] Updated changelogs and publish scripts
- [x] Documentation updates for auth precedence and streaming examples
- [x] Linear items linked: ENG-5234, ENG-5310

Testing notes: All unit tests for SDKs pass locally and in CI except one flaky e2e streaming test that was rerun and passed on the second attempt. Manual verification performed against the hosted staging endpoint to ensure headers and token refresh work across typical proxy setups.

Impact: This is non-breaking for most consumers; however, a small number of edge-case custom credential providers that relied on legacy init ordering may need to update to the new hooks (documented in the migration section below).

Migration notes (short):
- If you implement a custom TokenProvider, update to implement the refresh_async() / refresh() contract now used by the SDK wrapper.
- For streaming consumers: prefer the new async iterator / observable wrappers for simplified resource cleanup.

Related: see linear ENG-5234 (auth/retries unification) and ENG-5310 (streaming ergonomics).
